title: Safety bridge rollout: playbook & quick notes
content:
Context:
This is a personal scratchpad for an alternate approach to canarying: a "safety-bridge" pool that acts as an intermediary between old and new model variants. The idea is meant to reduce client cold-starts and KV-cache divergence while giving us tighter telemetry before broad flips.

Why a bridge? (motivating constraints)
- Long-lived sessions / client affinity (mobile agents) means simple fractional traffic splits produce noisy user-level signals.
- New model variant has noticeably different generation latency distribution; sudden flips create downstream tail latency regressions.
- We want deterministic failback (no partial state left on client side).

High-level plan (10k-foot):
1) Provision a small, dedicated bridge pool (size = 5% of expected steady qps).
2) Route only new-cohort clients and a tiny percentage of existing clients to the bridge.
3) Bridge runs both model versions in shadow for the first hour to capture token-level deltas, then serves new model actively for observed-safe cohorts.
4) Gradually expand cohort membership using telemetry gates.

Quick checklist (pre-roll)
- [ ] Confirm bridge pool capacity and instance types (ticket RDW-4827).
- [ ] Bake image with dual-model config and fallback hooks.
- [ ] Add lightweight rate limiter and per-client counters to avoid client floods.
- [ ] Update routing policy: add route rule "bridge-eligible" with client hashing (cookie/app-id).
- [ ] Create observability dashboard slices: bridge-vs-hosted latency, token-delta metric, error-by-client, cache-hit-rate.
- [ ] Attach tracing sampling for first 200 bridge requests.

Bridge behaviour details
- Session affinity: clients assigned to bridge get an affiliation cookie header "X-Roll-Bridge: <cohort-id>" for 12h by default. Affinity half-life: 6h — after that degrade to probabilistic assignment to avoid long pins.
- Shadowing window: for first hour bridge will issue a shadow call to the incumbent model and compute a token-delta score (distance metric on top-k tokens). Save deltas to ephemeral store for roll decision.
- Active serving: after a minimum observation window and no high-delta clusters, bridge flips to serve new model for that cohort.
- Fallback: any 5xx rate > 0.5% in 1m window or latency p99 > baseline + 250ms triggers immediate pinback of affected cohorts.

Telemetry gates (runtime)
- Gate A (safety): error_rate_bridge < 0.2% over 5m and p99_latency_bridge < baseline_p99 + 150ms.
- Gate B (quality): median token-delta < 0.12 and no concentrated token-delta clusters across top-50 prompts.
- Gate C (cost): average tokens/sec and GPU-util within predicted envelope (no >10% deviation).
- Gate D (client stretch): per-client failover count <= 2 in 24h.

Concrete rollout cadence (example)
- T+0: spin bridge pool, enable shadowing, route 1% new sessions from staging clients. Observe 30–60m.
- T+1h: if Gate A/B pass, flip those bridge-assigned sessions to active new model. Keep shadow copy for +2h.
- T+3h: expand bridge cohort by factor 3 (or to 5% qps) if gates still green.
- T+12h: open to 15% traffic across warm cohorts, maintain daily sanity checks for 72h.

Operational runbook (triage)
- Alert: bridge_error_rate > 0.5% for 3m -> Action: scale bridge down to 0.5x, enable route fallback to incumbent, page oncall SRE, capture 50 traces.
- Alert: token-delta spike on >5% prompts -> Action: pause bridge expansion, set shadow-only for suspect prompts, schedule model-quality review.
- Latency tail regression (p99 > baseline + 250ms) -> reduce batch sizes, enforce smaller max_seq config for bridge serving, consider CPU offload for preprocessing.

Pin/unpin guidance
- Pin new model to bridge cohorts only — do not pin globally until 24–72h of stable telemetry.
- If we unpin, ensure cookie-based affinity cleared by setting X-Roll-Bridge expiry to past and serve a short TTL so clients re-hash quickly.

Safety experiments to run (quick wins)
- Synthetic traffic with sticky sessions to measure effective cache-warm ratio between incumbent vs bridge.
- Inject 0.1% adversarial prompts from known failure classes to stress token-delta detector.
- Chaos: randomly drop 1% of bridge nodes to validate graceful fallback path.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to aggregate token-delta for multi-turn sessions? (per-turn vs rolling average) -- TODO: test weighting recent turns heavier.
- Should we enforce model config equivalence (quantization / temperature) across bridge and incumbent, or accept config diffs and treat them as known variance?
- Determine cost accounting: track bridge cost separately for chargeback to product.

Notes and quick commands
- Kill affinity for a cohort: curl -X POST $ROUTER/api/affinity/flush -d '{"cohort":"bridge-v1"}' (needs auth).
- Fetch last 200 token-delta events: sql: SELECT * FROM telemetry.token_deltas WHERE cohort='bridge-v1' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 200;

Post-roll checklist (after full flip)
- [ ] Audit client cookies, ensure no leftover stale affiliation headers.
- [ ] Sweep shadow logs and archive token-delta bucket to long-term store for model-regression investigations.
- [ ] Run quality eval set against production traffic examples and compare BLEU/ROUGE/LLR metrics.

Final notes (personal):
This is intentionally lightweight — goal is to have a coherent, low-friction path for teams that want to avoid mass-market flips but still need reasonably fast expansion. Bridge introduces some infra overhead but buys safer signal collection at user-granularity. Next iteration: prototype a small lib that encapsulates bridge-assignment logic so app teams can mark sessions "bridge-eligible" without changing router rules.

References: RDW-4827 (bridge infra), PR 821 (dual-model runtime), confluence page above for dashboards.
